opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
As Jesus is being crucified, a sign is placed above Him: “Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews.”

The religious leaders object. They want it changed.

Pilate refuses: “What I have written, I have written.”

He believes he is asserting control. He is not.

At the Cross—at the moment of our redemption—God is acting with full authority, precision, and intention. Even the actions of those who do not understand are being used to declare what is true.

Jesus is not losing His life. He is laying it down. Through His death, He conquers death.

Nothing about this is accidental. Nothing is rushed. Nothing is outside of God’s control.

That is the reality.

And yet we struggle to live within it.

We act as if everything depends on us—our timing, our decisions, our ability to hold things together. We feel pressure to move, to know, to control what comes next.

But the Cross proves otherwise.

God’s will is accomplished fully, even through human misunderstanding, resistance, and limitation. Pilate did not know what he was doing. Still, God’s purpose was carried out exactly.

So the question becomes:

Will we keep trying to control what was never ours to control?
Or will we learn to trust what God is already doing?

Scripture shows the pattern:
Moses waited 40 years.
David was anointed, then waited years to become king.
Jesus lived 30 years before His public ministry.

God is not rushed.

To live in that truth requires something difficult: surrender.

Not passivity, but trust.
Not inaction, but obedience without needing full clarity.

“Lie down in green pastures.”
“My yoke is easy.”

Rest is not the absence of movement.
It is the release of control.

The Cross has already shown us who is in control.

The question is whether we will live like we believe it.
